event.name: 8 January 2013 Lemnos Island (East Aegean Sea) earthquake
event.tectonic_setting: Dextral ENE–WSW trending strike-slip structure, eastward of the Agios Efstratios fault system; East Aegean Sea.
event.region: South of Lemnos Island, North Aegean Sea, Greece

reference.title: A study of the 8 January 2013 Mw5.8 earthquake sequence (Lemnos Island, East Aegean Sea)

inversion.method: Finite-fault inversion of regional 3-component broadband seismic waveforms using 1-km subfaults with slip positivity and smoothing constraints (Dreger-Kaverina style); Figure 5 colorbar digitized for the displayed window.
inversion.green_function_model: Green functions for 1-D velocity model in Novotny et al. (2001), as adopted for regional waveform modelling (refer to original paper).
inversion.notes: FIGURE-DIGITIZED RECONSTRUCTION, NOT ORIGINAL INVERSION COEFFICIENTS. Source: Kiratzi & Svigkas (2013), Figure 5 (p. 456), Tectonophysics 608, 452–460. Authors inverted a 20 x 20 km fault plane using 400 square 1 x 1 km subfaults, but published Figure 5 displays only a signed along-strike -4..+12 km / along-dip -5..+11 km WINDOW (16 x 16 km, 256 cells). JSON SEGMENT IS ONLY THE VISIBLE WINDOW: 256 measured pixels/area-averaged values, not 400 original coefficients. The 144 unshown subfaults have intentionally not been filled with invented zeros. Figure +x is toward SW despite the strike/dip input using 241 degrees SW; plotted +y is updip. JSON segment positive along_strike_km starts at local plotted -4 km (NE limit), positive down_dip_km starts at +11 km updip limit. Thus plotted x=JSON x-4, plotted along dip y=11-JSON down_dip. Hypocenter plotted (0,0) corresponds to local along-strike 4 km and down-dip 11 km; hypocenter absolute depth 11 km. Patch depth inferred as 11 - plotted_updip_km * sin(86 deg). Fault geographic reference point and per-patch lat/lon are null because image does not constrain fault-plane georeferencing. The PDF embeds a 693 x 873 pixel raster Figure 5; its slip colors were calibrated against the colorbar ~0-130 cm and spatially averaged within each visible 1-km cell, excluding dark grid strokes and the white hypocenter star. Values are rounded to 1 cm. Background violet estimates <3 cm were reported as 0-cm graphical baseline, not proof of exact physical zero slip. Cells near star and large within-cell gradients flagged in cell QA. The main patch spans ~7x8 km with paper-reported max 130 cm and mean ~30 cm over ruptured patch. The figure-derived MAX among displayed 1-km patch means is 123 cm; the displayed-window MEAN is 10.1 cm and is NOT comparable to the paper’s ruptured-patch mean 30 cm. The small secondary SW high-slip spot at positive x~8-9 km was reported unstable in trial inversions. Rise time 0.5 s and rupture velocity 2.6 km/s. Published seismic moment from slip model 6.4e24 dyn cm = 6.4e17 Nm. Original data are regional broadband waveforms; schema maps nonstandard waveform data type to other. No artificial interpolation was performed outside displayed area or across invisible original patches.

provenance.compiled_by: Figure 5 PNG extracted from author-provided PDF; image-to-colorbar per-pixel calibration, interior 1-km cell averaging and strict visible-window cropping; QA CSV and visual comparison.
